text:
mike: FYI alert for tenant acme-prod — multiple 429s across generation endpoints starting ~09:12 UTC. Customer reports degraded UX. Pls triage.

sre-bot: [alert] rate_limit_rejects > 100/min for tenant=acme-prod service=generation (triggered at 09:13 UTC)

anjali: looking. can someone paste a failing request/response?

mike: curl snippet from customer: ```curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` response: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1719004350
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded" }```

support-eng: customer says this started immediately after we rolled limiter policy 2024-11-02T09:10:00Z (burst window increase for acme-prod).

lisa: grabbing logs from edge and limiter nodes for that tenant now. Seen a few nodes with large burst grants then immediate zeros.

anjali: quick hypothesis: control-plane rollout changed policy units (sec vs ms) in new payload and some runtimes picked up stale cache of old policy -> token accounting mismatch. Could cause tokens to be consumed faster than expected.

mike: that matches what i see in node-17 logs: ``node=node-17 tenant=acme-prod policy_v=42 cached_v=41 refill=6000`` then later ``applied_refill=6`` — looks like unit mismatch.

lisa: repro steps I've been using locally: 1) apply new policy with refill=6000 (units=ms, intended 6s) 2) runtime reading as seconds => 6000 tokens instant refill -> allowed big burst -> downstream immediate throttles as token accounting clamps. I've got a trace.

anjali: ok, mitigation plan: (A) rollback policy change for acme-prod to previous stable until we fix unit parsing (B) invalidate policy caches in all runtime clusters (hot endpoint) (C) hotfix PR to normalize units and add strict schema validation on control plane payload.

devops: rolling cache invalidation now via /admin/policies/invalidate?tenant=acme-prod — running across regions. ETA ~4m.

support-eng: notified customer of investigation and provided temporary mitigation steps. They're open to a credit if this caused SLO hit.

mike: invalidate done in us-west-2. seeing drop in 429s on metrics dashboard. :thumbsup:

lisa: opened a hotfix branch (hotfix/limiter-unit-normalize). PR in progress, @anjali please review.

anjali: on it. will add strict unit test + e2e for policy rollouts. Also adding a canary gate in control plane to throttle rollout to 5% for 15m.

mike: created ticket INC-4821 for customer impact and credits. assigning follow-ups: @lisa telemetry to add a histogram of observed refill_delta and mismatches; @anjali implement unit schema + canary; @mike customer comms + postmortem.

devops: permanent mitigation noted: add cache-invalidate hook to the policy deploy flow and require backward-compatible unit fields.

lisa: capturing logs for postmortem: ``` limiter[node-17] policy_v=42 apply_time=1719004312 refill_config={"rate":10,"burst":60,"unit":"ms"} -> runtime_interpreted_unit="s" applied_refill=6000 -> tokens_after=0 ```

support-eng: customer reports improvement after invalidation. still monitoring.

mike: postmortem action items: - rollback may have avoided larger hit - ship hotfix within 24h - add alert on policy rollout -> sudden spike in refill_delta - update runbook for on-call to invalidate caches and check policy versions.

anjali: estimating 2-3 hours for hotfix + tests, then deploy to canary, then to prod. will update this thread with PR link.

lisa: PR opened: https://git.redwood/limiter/pull/915 — includes unit fixes and a parser that enforces ms/s explicitness.

mike: thanks. will draft public incident note for affected tenant and set follow-up meeting 10:30 UTC.

devops: closing alert for now; re-open if 429s reappear.

support-eng: leaving here for postmortem notes. will attach customer timeline once they confirm. :calendar:
